concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: Section 8.1 of the original DPA requires notification no later than 48 hours after awareness. Amendment No. 1 was signed on 15 September 2026 but its breach provisions take effect on 1 October 2026, so the 48-hour limit still applies on that date.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1, section A2.1, replaces Section 8.1 with a no-later-than 24-hour notification limit, effective 1 October 2026 and therefore in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1, section A3.1, reduces the on-site audit notice period under Section 10.2 from 30 days to 20 days, effective 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1, section A6.1, replaces Section 13.1 with a Processor liability cap of EUR 1,000,000 that is a fixed amount and does not depend on fees paid.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: Amendment No. 1, section A6.1, states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap shall not apply to breaches of Section 4 (Confidentiality), so the cap does not cover confidentiality breaches.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed as an approved Sub-processor in Annex 3, and its withdrawal under Amendment No. 1, section A4.1 takes effect only on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: Under Amendment No. 1, section A4.1, Meridian Mail Ltd's approval was withdrawn with effect from 1 January 2027, and the later emergency permission is limited to incident IR-27 in May 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, the countries with both processing and approval are Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, Denmark and France, since Ireland's Meridian approval was withdrawn and Denmark and France were added effective 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: Amendment No. 1, section A5.1, replaces the 90-day period in Section 12.1 with 60 days, and counting 60 calendar days from 31 December 2026 gives 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data it processes under the dpa. this 24-hour limit replaced the earlier 48-hour period.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting data it processes under the DPA. This 24-hour limit replaced the earlier 48-hour period.
justifications: This summary reflects Section 8.1 as replaced by Amendment No. 1, section A2.1, which was in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: Forensics confirmed usable privileged credentials were exposed, which triggers the 12-hour expedited outer limit for the breach. That limit runs from the original awareness and is not restarted by the later confirmation.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness occurred at 17:10 on 9 April 2027, so the 12-hour expedited limit expired at 05:10 on 10 April. The first notice was delivered at 06:00 that day, 50 minutes after that limit.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: The follow-up report is due at the end of the third Business Day after awareness on Friday 9 April 2027. Weekends and the 12 April closure are skipped, the Controller-approved 14 April pause is excluded, and the refused 16 April pause is not applied.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The later hold ends 25 August 2027, and the 60-day ordinary deadline is 29 August 2027. The end of the tenth Business Day after that release, excluding the 30 August closure, is 9 September 2027, which is later.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: BK-0630 was created on 30 June 2027 and contains no held records, so it must be deleted by the earlier of the ordinary deadline (29 August 2027) and 35 calendar days after creation (4 August 2027). Restoration does not restart this period.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: On 1 September 2027 the held ORD records remain under the deletion window following hold release, where they may be used only for legal preservation. The Controller rejected the request to use them for analytics, and service delivery is not permitted for held records.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval for the Stockholm infrastructure service begins no earlier than the latest of the proposed start date, security review completion, and written Controller consent. For Sweden, the security review completed on 22 April 2027, which is later than the 18 April consent and the 20 April start date.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS was added as an approved Sub-processor for transactional email delivery from 1 January 2027 and continues ordinary transactional email from France. Meridian Mail Ltd's approval was withdrawn, and its incident-only emergency permission does not cover ordinary customer email on 10 May 2027.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: These countries have both ongoing processing and effective authorisation on 15 May 2027: Norway storage continues, Estonia's Tallinn data centres continue under a renamed entity, Lithuania monitoring continues, France email continues, and Sweden infrastructure was approved and began processing. Denmark is excluded because its backup authorisation was withdrawn, and Ireland and Finland lack current authorised processing.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: The security cap is the greater of EUR 2,000,000 and twice Qualifying Fees. Qualifying Fees of EUR 1,140,000 (EUR 1,200,000 excluding VAT, less the EUR 60,000 service credit) make twice that EUR 2,280,000, which is the greater amount.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year, and EUR 300,000 of ordinary payments already consumed it in the Contract Year beginning 1 March 2027. Confidentiality and security payments do not consume this pool.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: L-1 is capped at the EUR 700,000 ordinary remainder. L-2 (EUR 1,750,000, counted once) fits within the EUR 1,780,000 security remainder, and L-3 and L-4 are confidentiality losses that are uncapped, giving EUR 250,000 and EUR 100,000 respectively.
